A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DE-MARK. Their complete main texts and appendices, including algorithms, equations, proofs, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite formatting and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark removal, exploitation, parameter-identification, ablation, and ChatGPT experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds WaterBench evaluations and removal experiments against two distortion-free watermark schemes.

M1.justification: Random selection probing, token scoring, parameter estimation, green-list identification, and removal/exploitation procedures are unchanged. v1 Algorithms 4–5 become v2 Algorithms 1–2 through relocation; testing additional watermark schemes does not document a procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds WaterBench Entity Probing, Concept Probing, and Long-form QA, substantially extending the original open-ended writing coverage to short-answer knowledge tasks and question answering. Tables 11–12 also extend removal evaluation to distortion-free gamma-reweight and DiPmark watermark environments.

E2.justification: No competing removal or stealing algorithm is added to the evaluated comparisons. Gamma-reweight and DiPmark are new watermark targets, with before-removal controls, rather than alternative removal methods. Pang et al. and Zhang et al. are discussed but explicitly not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: New WaterBench experiments use answer F1 or ROUGE-L and TPR at 10%, 1%, and 0.1% FPR; DiPmark experiments use 1%, 0.1%, and 0.01% FPR. These extend evaluation protocols without revising the retained experiments' models, generation settings, or metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused applicability check: whether removal works against distortion-free gamma-reweight and DiPmark, beyond the original additive red/green watermark design. The eta ablation, parameter-identification analyses, and ChatGPT case study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports across-run confidence intervals or variability estimates, and v2 introduces no new seed or repeated-run reporting. Additional detector p-values follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 7, 11, and 12 add substantive results for new tasks and watermark schemes. For example, the new Llama3.1 Long-form QA experiment reports 91% TPR at 0.1% FPR before removal versus 0.5% with DE-MARK. Existing Tables 1–4 and v1 Tables 7–9 retain their numerical values, with the latter renumbered 8–10.

T1.justification: Section 4.1.1 replaces Gaussian noise with a general symmetric-noise assumption. The Theorem 4.1 proof correspondingly drops the Gaussian specification while retaining its symmetry argument. The theorem statements, removal bound, and remaining derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: watermark parameter recovery without prior parameter knowledge, removal with distributional guarantees, and exploitation. Added experiments support these claims without redefining the advertised contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly interprets short-answer results as showing greater watermark-induced quality damage and recovery of the original distribution through DE-MARK. Existing access/query-cost limitations and removal-quality tradeoffs remain unchanged; the main-text Impact Statement repeats an existing risk discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract. Prompts, model identifiers, top-20 access, generation settings, and hyperparameters were already documented in v1; their repetition in Section 5 is not new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds watermark-detection and image-watermark-removal literature, and distinguishes Pang et al.'s detector-access setting and Zhang et al.'s unigram setting. WaterBench and other citations are added, while several general broader-impact references are removed or replaced. The original positioning against Jovanovic et al. remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved. Limited structural edits move algorithm listings into the main text, repeat experimental-setting summaries in Section 5, expand related work, add a main-text Impact Statement and acknowledgments, and renumber appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICML layout throughout, changing typography, headers, captions, spacing, and placement. It adds three result tables, moves two appendix algorithm listings into the main text, and systematically adds directional arrows and bold result highlighting. Existing Figures 1–7 retain their content.

improvement.justification: WaterBench and distortion-free watermark evaluations provide useful evidence beyond v1's writing tasks and original watermark design. The code pointer and clearer related-work distinctions also improve usability. These gains are tempered by sparse details for the new experiments and a short-answer distribution-recovery interpretation that Table 7 does not directly establish: it lacks an unwatermarked reference and shows mixed quality changes.
